title: Stone_Feature
description: An extensive archaeological Tel buried under Roman-Byzantine ruins. Features major adjacent Iron Age slag heaps, pottery scatters, and agricultural fields 2. Faynan 5 is the second-largest smelting site in the region with ~30,000 tons of slag, showing furnace and tap slag, tuyères, and 8th-century BCE installations 4.

description: Located in the "Northwest cemetery" of Khirbat Faynan 8. Features thin plate slag and small reed-impressed tuyères identical to those of Late Bronze Age Timna Site 30 8.

title: Agriculture
description: Extensive field terraces containing scatters of Iron Age pottery, representing agricultural activity supporting the smelting population 9.

title: Mining
description: Features 14 blackish mining waste dumps from shafts dug into the lower Umm Ishrin formation to reach the buried Burj (DLS) ore body below 9.

title: Mining
description: A model mining district studied by the GMM containing 56 recorded mines 10. Features double shafts dug through the Umm Ishrin formation to exploit deeper Burj (DLS) ore 10. Mine 42 was active in the LBA 12, while WF 1422 features both Iron Age double shafts and a Roman prospection shaft 11.

title: Smelting
description: Located on a hilltop mountain pass 15. Features a 100-ton heap of slag reprocessed and remelted during the Iron Age II to extract metal inclusions, along with rock-cut cup marks for slag crushing 15.

title: Smelting
description: One of the largest smelting centers in the Levant, featuring dozens of slag mounds (~50,000–60,000 tons of slag) 16. Includes a 73x73m fortress, monumental buildings, a gatehouse converted to a smelting workshop (Area A), and a highly specialized refining workshop (Area F) 16.

title: Smelting
description: Extensive unfortified smelting site on both sides of Wadi al-Jariya containing 15,000–20,000 tons of slag 19. Represents the early, unfortified phase of Iron Age smelting before the consolidation at KEN 19.

title: Mining
description: Surveyed wadi valley featuring ~50 recorded mines, at least 26 of which yielded Iron Age pottery 20. Mines consist of shafts dug into the Umm Ishrin sandstone to exploit the buried Burj (DLS) formation 20.

title: Smelting

title: Smelting
description: Features extensive scatters of small slag fragments on both sides of Wadi al-Ghuweiba 24. Excavation revealed an Iron Age I–IIA smelting layer underneath a later Roman-Nabataean building 24.

title: Burial
description: The western gateway to the Faynan district 23. Surveyed sectors documented cemeteries, campsites, and several small-scale copper smelting scatters demonstrating simpler technologies than the major lowland centers 23.

title: Smelting
description: The largest Early Bronze Age copper manufactory in the Near East 28. However, it features a large eastern surface "slag mound" confirmed by archaeomagnetism and radiocarbon to date to the Iron Age I 28.

title: Burial
description: The largest Iron Age cemetery in Edom (~3,450 m²) with an estimated 1,500 to 3,000 sub-surface cist graves 30. Attributed to a mobile nomadic community (Shasu) whose members were actively engaged in smelting 30.

title: Burial
description: Well-preserved EBI village and metalworking site 32. Reused during the Iron Age for isolated tumuli burials, including Tomb 1 which contained eight individuals buried with Egyptian amulets 32.

title: Mining
description: Small mining district with 24 tailing dumps 33. Shafts were dug into the local gravel to reach the buried Burj (DLS) formation 33. Probably supplied ore to Wadi Fidan's smelting sites 33.

title: Mining_Field_Placer
description: Located near Jabal Madsus, containing 20–30 refilled pit mines ("Tellerpingen") and a nearby early smelting installation 34.

title: Smelting
description: Located far from the mines 35. Features an excavated "four-room" house (BH2) containing Midianite pottery and limited smelting remains, serving as an oasis road station on the route leading to the Gulf of Aqaba 35.

title: Smelting
description: Structural remains situated on a small, prominent inselberg 37. It is unique as the only stratified site in the Edom lowlands preserving clear evidence of both 10th-century and 7th–6th-century BCE occupations 38.

title: Mining_Field_Placer
description: A massive mining district consisting of three fields of pit mines (JAJ-1, 2, 3) in the colluvial/alluvial deposits of the Burj (DLS) formation, associated with a geological dike 39. It served as the main ore source for Khirbat en-Nahas 39.
